o.text: From Old Anatolian Turkish چادر (çadïr, “tent”), from Proto-Oghuz *čādïr (“tent”), from Proto-Common Turkic *čātïr (“tent”), possibly from Middle Persian [Book Pahlavi needed] (cʾtwl /⁠čādur⁠/), ultimately from Sanskrit छत्त्र (chattra, “parasol, umbrella, awning”)

glosses: inconsolable (only with nouns denoting seat of emotion: sinəsi, ürəyi, qəlbi)

o.text: From Proto-Turkic *yegit, *yigit (“young man, brave man”). See Turkish yiğit for more cognates.

From yağ + -la.
Third sense is perhaps a semantic loan from Russian умасли́ть (umaslítʹ).
